title: Matthias (14 May)
hookLine: the apostle chosen by lot to replace Judas

cards: An upper room in Jerusalem, after the ascension. The apostles are waiting, praying, and there's an empty place among them. Judas is gone.

Peter stands up and says the place has to be filled. Not by just anyone: by someone who has walked with them the whole way, from John's baptism to the day Jesus was taken up. Two names are put forward.
Then, instead of a vote or a speech, they do something that may sound strange.

teach.h: TWO NAMES, A PRAYER, A LOT.
teach.b: Here's how Acts tells it. The two men are Joseph called Barsabas, also named Justus, and Matthias. The apostles pray, asking the Lord, who knows every heart, to show which one he has chosen.
Then they cast lots. In the Douay-Rheims: "And they gave them lots, and the lot fell upon Matthias, and he was numbered with the eleven apostles." That's it.
Three things stand out. First, the qualification. Matthias wasn't new.
He'd been there all along, through the roads and the crowds and the cross, without ever being named.
He was a witness before he was an apostle. Second, the lot.
Acts presents it as a way of leaving the choice to God: they prayed first, then let the answer fall.

Some readers notice that after the Spirit comes at Pentecost, a few verses later, Acts never shows the apostles choosing this way again. Third, the silence. After this verse, Acts doesn't mention Matthias again.
Tradition tells stories of where he preached, but the text gives him one moment, and not an easy one.

teach.h: HE FILLS A PLACE LEFT BY BETRAYAL.
teach.b: He takes the place of a betrayer, filling a gap left by grief and scandal. Catholics honor him as a full apostle anyway. Not a substitute.
The one the lot fell on, who had been quietly faithful long before anyone wrote his name down.

how: Catholics keep the feast of Saint Matthias on 14 May, reading the account of his choosing from Acts 1 at Mass.

games.q: you're one of the eleven. there are two good men for one empty place. how do you choose?
o: take a vote and go with the majority.
games.why: they prayed, cast lots, and the lot fell upon Matthias. he was numbered with the eleven.

practice: Bring to mind a place you've ended up that you didn't choose: covering for someone who left, caring for a parent, a job that fell to you because nobody else would take it.

Notice how it feels to stand in someone else's spot, and then what you'd been doing quietly before that made you ready for it. If you pray, offer that role to God as it is; if you don't, simply let yourself accept it for now.
